answer: A practical Sybil defence is weighted admission: an identity counts only after it posts a bond that is slashed for bad behaviour and earns reputation slowly through graded work. Clones gain nothing by multiplying, since each one pays the same entry cost and arrives at zero reputation, so no free haven exists for throwaway accounts. A cheap relic from an earlier epoch cannot be reused, because scores decay and must be re-earned. With admission priced above expected reward per clone, mass registration loses money and honest weight dominates the horizon of influence.
